newsitem.title: INDIA: India bullion closes up on low stock, world trends.
newsitem.headline: India bullion closes up on low stock, world trends.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees higher at 4,630 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,625 rupees amid limited arrivals and stray speculative support.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees higher at 54,200 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Thursday.

** Silver (.999) closed 45 rupees higher at 6,770 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,725 rupees as rally in the world market and shortage of ready stock helped local prices to bounce back. Silver was down by 15 rupees per kg on Thursday.
Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees higher at 4,630 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,625 rupees amid limited arrivals and stray speculative support on Friday, dealers said.
Gold was down by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Thursday. Physical buying however remained at a low ebb and volume was slow during the day.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees higher at 54,200 rupees per piece after losing 200 rupees on Thursday.
"Sentiment at the close remained subdued on reports of a fresh setback in the world market," one broker said.

Silver (.999) closed 45 rupees higher at 6,770 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,725 rupees amid a shortage of ready stock while an uptrend in the world market triggered speculative buying. Silver was down 15 rupees on Thursday.
"Physical demand from industrial consumers was dull during the day and we have witnessed only speculative enquiries," a broker added.
